An audit · 158 lines · at commit 4427cbe

HoloTable against SW5e what a table needs to play the whole system, and what is there

This is a line-by-line check of HoloTable, the Star Wars 5e tabletop jpesus built on the Den, against what the SW5e rules ask of a table: making and levelling characters, class resources, powers, the sheet's arithmetic, gear, rests and conditions, combat on the map, the GM's side, starships, downtime, and the table itself. It describes HoloTable's code at commit 4427cbe (17 Nov 2026, 08:01 PST), so anything changed since then is not counted. It is meant as a to-do list for the group, not a verdict.

  • 63 ✓ done
  • 35 ◐ partial
  • 60 ✗ missing

The ten gaps that matter most

  1. Class resources (3.1–3.11). No class's spendable numbers are tracked: rages, superiority dice, focus points, exploits, Channel the Force, Second Wind, Action Surge, Indomitable, Potent Aptitude, Kinetic Combat, Ranger's Quarry, Sage Advice and the rest. Every class has some, and they are spent every session.
  2. Rests recover the wrong things (7.2–7.5). Tech points should come back on a short rest and don't. The Consular's Force Recovery and every short-rest class use (Channel the Force, Action Surge, Second Wind and the like) aren't there, and hit dice are spent from one pool at the largest die size.
  3. Caster numbers that are wrong today (3.12–3.14). The Sentinel's max power level is one too low at nine of its twenty levels. The 12 archetypes that grant casting get no points. A multiclassed caster's max power level uses the wrong rule.
  4. Measuring and areas on the map (8.4, 8.5). There's no ruler and no cone, cube, cylinder, line or sphere template, and both are needed in every fight.
  5. SW5e's own conditions, with effects and durations (7.7–7.10). Five of SW5e's 21 conditions are missing, exhaustion follows the wrong table, and no condition changes a roll or ends on its own.
  6. Casting beyond spending points (4.4–4.7). Upcasting, the max power level check, concentration, and rolling a power's damage and its targets' saves are all missing.
  7. Attack to damage on a target (8.6, 5.10, 9.6). You can't pick a target, roll against its AC and apply the damage with its resistances. Today the GM copies numbers from chat into the tracker.
  8. The sheet's typed numbers (5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.8, 5.9). AC isn't derived from armor and shields, there's no toggle for weapon proficiency, there's no box for misc bonuses, weapon properties have no mechanics, and feature damage (rage, Sneak Attack and so on) isn't offered on rolls.
  9. Building and choosing (1.3, 1.7, 1.8, 2.7, 2.9). There's no level-1 build. Background skills aren't ticked and the background feat is never added. A character past level 3 can't pick an archetype. The per-level choices (maneuvers, exploits, ideals, styles, expertise) are never asked for or counted.
  10. Creatures beyond hit points (9.4–9.7). Legendary actions, recharge and per-day abilities aren't tracked, saves and skills can't be rolled, resistances aren't applied, and there's no encounter difficulty.

Next after these: starship combat as its own system (10.5–10.11), Wretched Hives modifications and attunement (6.3, 6.4), downtime and factions (11.1–11.3), encumbrance (6.5).

Done well

  • Server-side dice and private play. Rolls are made on the server. GM-only rolls, whispers to a character, hidden NPCs and hidden ships are all handled, and players are never sent what they shouldn't see. The tests check this.
  • SW5e content in place. Every book's lists are fetched by the server, cached with size caps and credited. The pickers cover powers, gear, enhanced items, species, backgrounds, feats, maneuvers, fighting styles and masteries, lightsaber forms, ventures and archetypes. The full rulebooks are searchable in the library, and the GM marks which variant rules the table uses.
  • The level-up wizard. It runs on GM grants. It handles average, rolled or maximum HP with retroactive Con, gives ASIs at the right class levels (all ten classes checked against SW5e's tables), picks the archetype at 3 and adds each level's features.
  • Caster arithmetic for single-class Consular, Engineer, Guardian and Scout. Point totals, max power level, point costs, and DCs and attack bonuses by alignment all match SW5e.
  • Ship arithmetic that matches Starships of the Galaxy. Ship skills with crew proficiency, weapon attack on Wisdom and damage on Strength, and shields taking damage before hull.
  • Import from the sw5e.com builder and Foundry. It flags what the player needs to check.
  • Saving that doesn't lose a game. It saves on every change, keeps a backup every ten minutes of play, exports with images, restores, and never saves a blank table over a lost one.
  • Scum and Villainy at the GM's fingertips. 271 creatures go into the tracker with tokens, HP and AC, and their attacks roll privately from the stat block.
  • Map and scenes. Pan, zoom and pinch, Dungeondraft packs, and named scenes that switch every screen at once.
  • Tests. 45 server tests cover security, privacy, saving and the rules engine, and all pass at 4427cbe.

How this was checked
  • HoloTable: every line of the files above was read at 7b5f7c0, and the diffs of the two later commits were checked for anything that touches a line here. The test suite was run locally: 42 of 42 pass at 7b5f7c0, 43 of 43 at 91c959c, 45 of 45 at 4427cbe. Line numbers below are at 4427cbe. The live site was not opened (it is behind two passwords this audit did not use), so nothing here says what the live game currently holds.
  • SW5e: from SW5e's own public data (sw5eapi.azurewebsites.net), fetched for this audit: the class tables (class), archetypes (archetype), creatures (monster), size data (starshipBaseSize), and the chapter lists of the Player's Handbook (playerHandbookRule), Starships of the Galaxy (starshipRule), Wretched Hives (wretchedHivesRule), the Expanded Content (expandedContent) and the Variant Rules (variantRule).
  • SW5e's API reports one data version for everything it serves: version 199, last updated 6 May 2023. HoloTable's pickers and library show that build, so anything sw5e.com changed later is not in them.
  • A fuller inventory of SW5e's data was built for this audit (sw5e-inventory.md, kept with it). Every count quoted below from that inventory was re-checked against the API before use.
  • A line marked (inferred) is a judgement not read directly from code or from SW5e's data.

The full audit as written: audit.md (also on GitHub). This page is built from it by build.mjs, so the two say the same thing.

The rules named here belong to SW5e (sw5e.com). This page names rules and points at HoloTable's code; it copies none of the rules' text. HoloTable is jpesus's.
